description: The three forms of video Motion Lab produces, and only these: short-form (micro explainers), mid-form (focused explainers) and long-form (documentaries and deep dives). A brief declares one in deliverables.video_type; scripts/studio.py new requires it and validate enforces it. Any form can be a member of a series (specs/series-spec.json), alone or mixed with the others. Each form has its own playbook skill (.claude/skills/short-form, mid-form, long-form) for storytelling, scripting, pacing and editing; subject knowledge (history, technology, science, finance, ...) comes from categories and style templates, not from the form. Guide: docs/video-forms.md.
aliases_note: Ids used before spec 2.0.0 (2026-11-08). Briefs, series files and CLI flags that still say reel, long-reel or youtube are read as short, mid and long; new work should use the new ids. reel -> short is exact. long-reel -> mid is exact for length; mid may now also be landscape. youtube -> long only when the film is 5 minutes or more; a legacy 3-5 minute YouTube film has no form and must be re-typed as mid (shorten) or long (extend).
margin_note: Each nominal range may be missed by this many seconds at either end. The allowed window is nominal.min - margin to nominal.max + margin, but never below window_floor_sec when a form sets one. Windows therefore leave 195-285 s unassigned on purpose: a film that long is either a long mid-form film (cut it) or a short long-form film (build it out).
complexity_note: complexity_budget is what one film of the form can explain (story-writer rulebook 3.1, scope check, added 2026-11-07 from the owner's review of game-theory-trust: 'We can't compress complicated content into a short video.'). A mechanism is a cause-and-effect chain the viewer must follow to reach the payoff. A new term is a concept name, a jargon word, or a named person, study, event, tournament or algorithm the audience must learn; names that appear only in a source line do not count. A named study, event, tournament or algorithm needs its setup (who, what, how it was scored, what happened, why), at least named_case_setup_sec_min seconds. Over budget: cut, split into a series, or move to a longer form. The short-form numbers are the owner's ruling; the mid-form and long-form numbers are a first guess, not yet measured on a finished film.

render_segments.note: A film longer than above_sec is rendered in segments of about segment_sec, cut at scene edges, with a checkpoint after each and a resume after an interrupted build (scripts/render-segments.py, called by studio.py build). Shorter films render in one pass. Chosen for the 8 GB M2: a segment bounds one headless-Chrome session to about 2,700 frames. Not yet measured on a 12-minute film; adjust segment_sec from logs/build-timings.jsonl.

short.name: Short-form
short.subtitle: Micro explainer
short.summary: One interesting idea, fact, discovery or insight. Fast, visually dense, one satisfying takeaway.

complexity_budget.named_case_rule: only as the film's whole subject; never a closing beat or a re-hook

short.note: 45 s is preferred; go toward 60 s only for a complicated topic that needs more animated beats, not more words. Under about 35 s there is no room for a named case, so the film is a single fact or number.

mid.name: Mid-form
mid.subtitle: Focused explainer
mid.summary: One concept, process, event or question explained in real depth without becoming a documentary.
mid.structure: Hook -> Context -> Explanation -> Visual demonstration -> Conclusion

complexity_budget.alternative: two linked mechanisms and no worked case

mid.note: Portrait (Instagram) or landscape (YouTube, LinkedIn); the brief picks one and a mid-form film is rendered in that one format only. Portrait needs a re-hook about every 35-45 s; landscape about every 45-60 s. Reel-loop fits only the short end.

long.name: Long-form
long.subtitle: Documentary or deep dive
long.summary: A narrative-driven film on a complex subject, event, discovery, paper or set of linked ideas. Storytelling, depth, accuracy and an immersive picture.
long.structure: Hook -> Context -> Narrative development -> Deep explanation -> Resolution
long.formats_note: Portrait long-form was allowed by the owner on 2026-11-09 for the first upper-body workout film (720x1280); landscape stays the default for documentaries.

chapters.note: Every long-form film is a list of chapters (storyboard.json `chapters`). A chapter is the unit of structure, of the complexity budget, of the re-hook, of the frame-review contact sheet and of the render checkpoint.

long.note: Landscape by default (portrait when the brief asks, owner ruling 2026-11-09), 5-12 minutes (4:45 to 12:15 with the margin). Needs a cold open that earns the first minute, a re-hook every 60-90 s, descriptive chapter titles (they become the YouTube chapters) and a resolution that answers the cold open. A long-form film is never re-rendered at 9:16; its reels and shorts are separate short-form films made around its strongest single insight.
